workflow.obligation_text:
REs shall,
(a) maintain all necessary records of transactions between the RE and the 
customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date 
of transaction;
workflow.policy_text:
The bank shall maintain records of domestic and international customer
transactions for at least five years from the transaction date.

workflow.obligation_text:
REs shall,
(a) maintain all necessary records of transactions between the RE and the 
customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date 
of transaction;
workflow.policy_text:
The bank shall preserve customer identification and address records
for at least five years after the customer relationship ends.

deterministic.attribute_explanation: The policy does not establish the required record or activity scope.
deterministic.retention_explanation: The policy specifies a minimum of 5 years, meeting the extracted regulatory minimum of 5 years. Only the duration was compared; scope, start event, and exceptions remain unverified.

result.regulatory_quote: maintain all necessary records of transactions between the RE and the customer, both domestic and international, for at least five years from the date of transaction
result.policy_quote: The bank shall preserve customer identification and address records for at least five years after the customer relationship ends.

comparisons.regulatory_requirement: all necessary records of transactions between the RE and the customer, both domestic and international
comparisons.assessment: The policy covers identification and address records, whereas the regulation mandates transaction records.
Both specify a minimum duration of five years.
The triggers are different; the regulation triggers from the transaction date, while the policy triggers from the end of the relationship.

missing_requirements: The policy does not explicitly mention the retention of transaction records.
The policy does not define the retention start event as the date of the transaction.
potential_conflicts: The policy's retention trigger (end of relationship) differs from the regulatory requirement (date of transaction), which may lead to non-compliance if the relationship lasts longer than the transaction date.
result.explanation: The policy focuses on customer identification and address records, while the regulation specifically mandates the retention of transaction records. Furthermore, the retention triggers are fundamentally different, meaning the policy does not satisfy the regulatory requirement for transaction record retention.
